text:
maya: quick heads-up 1 prototyped a 'transfer-token' flow for multi-region cutovers. Goal: avoid full snapshot replay for small tenants and reduce egress. gist: issue a signed, short-lived capability the target region can accept, then flip ownership after a lightweight handshake.
jordan: short summary ok, but how do we avoid split-brain / lost-writes? we need clear liveness/consistency guarantees.
maya: model: origin keeps serving reads until claim completes. target can start accepting writes in a shadow-forward mode: writes are applied locally and forwarded to origin for durability until claim confirmed. If claim fails, local shadow-writes are either tombstoned or replayed to origin depending on policy.
anita: for billing/compliance we must ensure every accepted write has an immutable audit event. where do those events live?
maya: audit-wire emits a lifecycle event for every token action (create/query/accept/abort) plus a per-write trace id. retention and export hooks will be part of the RFC.
sam: what's the TTL? GC interactions? we can't let tokens expire while snapshot GC windows still accept writes.
maya: default TTL=90s, operator can set 30s	10m. we gate token issuance if cluster GC horizon < ttl + safety_margin.
elio: client SDKs: do we change retry semantics? older SDKs might not understand the handshake.
maya: SDKs: if target doesn't return "accepted" we fallback to origin and surface transient 409 to clients. For control-plane incompatibility (old region can't verify token) we fallback to full safety-escrow flow.
jordan: console/ops: what states show up? we need a concise state machine for oncall.
maya: planned states: TRANSFER_PENDING, TRANSFER_ACTIVE (target serving), TRANSFER_ABORTED, TRANSFER_REPLAYING. ops-bot will post each transition with tenant id + trace.
ops-bot: automsg 1 transfer-token: created tenant=globex ttl=90s trace=tx-993
jordan: can you paste the API sketch so infra can reason about auth/compat?
maya: pasted rough gRPC below (very small):

```
service TransferCoordinator {
  rpc CreateToken(CreateTokenReq) returns (TransferToken);
  rpc QueryToken(TokenQueryReq) returns (TokenStatus);
  rpc AcceptToken(AcceptReq) returns (AcceptResp);
  rpc AbortToken(AbortReq) returns (AbortResp);
}

message TransferToken { string id; int64 expires_at; string base_seq; repeated string flags; string signature; }
```

sam: couple engineering notes:
- need KMS-signed tokens and replay-resistant nonce.
- ensure token verification doesn't require global clock synchrony (use expiry + nonce + signature).
- record token actions in audit index for quick queries.
elio: failure modes: what if network partition prevents origin acknowledgements but target thinks it's accepted? monotonicity risk.
maya: we won't mark TRANSFER_ACTIVE until origin ACKs a short-chain proof: origin issues an accept-ack anchored to its commit log. Claim requires that ack or manual operator override.
anita: testing: run simnet with cross-region blackhole + fast-forward writer. measure tail-latency and assert no acknowledged writes are lost.
sam: quick perf numbers from local sim: for tenants <25qps and state <2MB, median cutover latency drops from ~8s (escrow) to ~0.9s (token), egress down ~92%. large/high-qps tenants still prefer full escrow.
jordan: feature controls? we need per-tenant opt-out and a cluster master switch.
maya: yes 1 per-tenant feature flag + cluster-level toggle. also a circuit-breaker: if we see >1% failed claims in a rollout, disable token issuance automatically.
elio: add compatibility story to RFC: older control-planes fall back to escrow, and SDKs incrementally enable optimistic-accept path.
maya: will draft RFC with sequence diagrams, event schema, and operator runbook. will include a small safety shim for runtime upgrades.
ops-bot: automsg 1 audit-event logged token.create tenant=globex id=tx-993 user=maya
jordan: cool. @maya when RFC is up drop link here and ping infra + devex for SDK changes. :thumbsup:
